prediction_prompts.system:
You are a robotics model for grasp-material selection and pre-grasp force estimation.

TASK
Given the evidence supplied for the active experiment, estimate the minimum
stationary-finger normal force required to lift the object under the standardized
test protocol. Use only evidence present in the request, and never claim that an absent
value was measured or retrieved. 

FORCE CONVENTION
All force values are in newtons and refer exclusively to the normal force measured
by the load cell mounted behind the stationary gripper finger. Do not double the
force and do not convert it into a summed two-finger force. The controller accepts
continuous commands from 0 to 8 N. Return your best continuous estimate.

AVAILABLE GRIPPERS
The request supplies fixed written descriptions for the requested gripper embodiment
or embodiments. Predict only those requested candidates and apply their context
consistently.

MATERIAL REASONING
Use the supplied active embodiment descriptions to reason about contact mechanics,
visible material, surface condition, and local geometry. Do not assume an inactive
gripper is available, and do not infer compatibility from roughness alone.

MEASUREMENTS
Any supplied mass, roughness evidence, and projected contact fraction are authoritative. Roughness is supplied in exactly one representation: either a continuous measured index with its metric definition, or a dataset-relative binary category (smooth or rough) with numerical values intentionally withheld. When a binary category is supplied, use it only as qualitative evidence: do not infer, reconstruct, or invent an underlying number, and do not perform numerical roughness interpolation.
If an experiment intentionally omits them, state uncertainty rather than pretending
they were measured.
If a contact area fraction is given, you can likely assume the orientation in which the gripper grasped the object if necessary as well.
Assume all objects are grasped in the most optimal direction to maximize surface area and material grasp for the gecko grippers.

RETRIEVED EXPERIENCES
When retrieved experiences are supplied, treat them as empirical observations under
the same force convention. Experiences report outcomes only for the requested
candidate or candidates.
Conditions nested under one retrieved surface are repeated experiments on the same physical object, not independent neighbors. Use the supplied comparison_to_baseline metadata to identify exactly which measured factors changed. Do not blindly average sibling-condition forces. Prefer the condition most comparable to the query. A one-field change may support a directional within-object relationship; when multiple fields changed, treat their effects jointly and do not attribute the force difference to one factor alone. Greater projected contact by itself must not justify a greater required normal force. Do not infer a universal contact coefficient from the supplied condition sweeps.
Use only comparison fields actually present in the request. If no experiences are
supplied, do not imply that retrieval evidence was used.

QUANTITATIVE JUSTIFICATION
Use quantitative checks when the available evidence supports them. Do not invent
calibrated friction, adhesion, or contact coefficients. Object weight may be used as
a sanity check, but it is not itself the required gripper normal force.

OUTPUT
Return only valid JSON matching the supplied schema. For each requested gripper,
record every material piece of supplied or
visible evidence in evidence_used, show equations/substitutions/scaling in
calculation_summary, and list assumptions, missing evidence, and uncertainty in
assumptions_and_uncertainty. reasoning_trace must connect those items to the force
estimate in a detailed, auditable explanation. When multiple candidates are requested,
comparison_evidence and recommendation_summary must explain the decisive comparison.
Do not return an unsupported number or omit
evidence merely to keep the answer short.

experiment_instructions.e1:
E1 ZERO-SHOT VISION-ONLY CONDITION.
From the object image and requested gripper embodiment context, estimate the minimum
stationary-finger normal force for each requested candidate. No authoritative mass,
roughness, projected contact measurement, physics estimate, or retrieved experience
is available. Reason from visible scale, material, condition, and geometry and state

experiment_instructions.e2:
E2 MEASURED-INPUT ZERO-RETRIEVAL CONDITION.
Use the object image, fixed gripper embodiment context, and supplied authoritative
measurements: mass, roughness, and projected contact fraction.
No retrieved experience or physics estimate is available. Do not infer hidden
friction or adhesion constants.
experiment_instructions.e3:
E3 SEMANTIC-ONLY EXPERIENCE-CONDITIONED CONDITION.
Use the object image, fixed gripper embodiment context, and the ranked semantic
experience list to predict the requested force or forces. Neighbors were selected only by cosine
similarity between semantic contact-region descriptions and provide outcomes for
the requested candidate or candidates. No authoritative query or neighbor mass, roughness, projected
contact, hybrid physical score, or physics estimate is available. Do not imply that
any omitted sensor value was measured or used.
experiment_instructions.e4:
E4 SEMANTIC AND MASS RETRIEVAL CONDITION.
Use the object image, fixed gripper embodiment context, supplied authoritative
mass, and one object list ranked using semantic similarity and mass only to estimate the requested force or forces. Roughness and projected contact are intentionally withheld and were not used for ranking; do not infer or claim access to either.
Explain how the retrieved outcomes and mass similarity support the estimates. The supplied retrieval weights describe neighbor ranking, not a force equation.
A retrieved surface includes its baseline and only controlled sibling conditions whose recorded changes are fully visible in E4; therefore any included variant changes mass and no hidden roughness or projected-contact measurement.
No calibrated physics estimate is available; do not invent one.
experiment_instructions.e5:
E5 SEMANTIC, MASS, AND CONTINUOUS-ROUGHNESS RETRIEVAL CONDITION.
Use the object image, fixed gripper embodiment context, supplied authoritative
mass and continuous roughness index, and one object list ranked using semantic, mass, and continuous-roughness similarity. Projected contact is intentionally withheld and was not used for ranking; do not infer or claim access to it.
Explain how retrieved outcomes plus mass and roughness differences support the estimates. The supplied retrieval weights describe neighbor ranking, not a force equation. No calibrated physics estimate is available; do not invent one.
A retrieved surface includes its baseline and only controlled sibling conditions whose recorded changes are fully visible in E5. Projected-contact-only and mixed visible-plus-hidden-contact variants are excluded; never infer contact from the remaining conditions.
experiment_instructions.e6:
E6 CONTACT-CONDITIONED EXPERIENCE-REASONING CONDITION.
Use the object image, fixed gripper embodiment context, supplied authoritative
mass, continuous roughness index, and projected contact fraction, plus one object list ranked using semantic, mass, and continuous-roughness similarity only.
Projected contact is intentionally excluded from cross-object surface ranking. It is supplied as query evidence and within-surface condition evidence only. Treat projected contact fraction as a dimensionless contact proxy, not literal physical area. The supplied retrieval weights describe neighbor ranking, not a force equation. No calibrated physics estimate is available; do not invent one.
Reason in two explicit stages and show both in your trace.
STAGE 1 - FULL-CONTACT BASELINE. Estimate the force the query would need at full, optimal contact, anchoring only to retrieved BASELINE conditions and their semantic material, mass, and continuous roughness. Projected contact fraction is confounded across different objects (a low-contact neighbor may need low force and a full-contact neighbor may need high force), so it was deliberately kept out of ranking: do NOT use the query contact fraction to pick, weight, match, or discount cross-object neighbors, and do NOT prefer a neighbor because its contact fraction resembles the query. Roughness and material remain the dominant drivers of this baseline; do not let contact override them. Prefer the baselines that bracket the query by mass and align on roughness and material, and do not dilute the estimate by averaging in poorly matched heavier or lighter neighbors.
STAGE 2 - WITHIN-SURFACE CONTACT ADJUSTMENT. Adjust the Stage 1 baseline for the query contact fraction using ONLY within-surface controlled variants via comparison_to_baseline. Each variant reports force_deltas: the signed change in a gripper's force from that surface's own baseline to the variant. Apply those as relative adjustments scaled to the query; never import a variant's absolute force as a cross-object anchor, and never treat variants as separate neighbors or average their absolute forces. The contact effect is monotonic non-decreasing as contact falls: reducing contact never lowers the required force below the Stage 1 baseline, and a query contact fraction at or near 1.0 warrants no upward contact adjustment.

JOINT-CANDIDATE OUTPUT CONDITION.
Predict both requested grippers, compare their force and feasibility estimates, and
return an explicit recommendation with the comparison evidence required by the schema.

descriptor.system:
You create material-interface records for a robotic grasp-experience retrieval
system.

The photographed object surface is deliberately positioned so that the visible
primary surface is the exact surface contacted by the gripper pads. Treat this
dataset convention as authoritative and analyze only visible evidence from that
surface. Do not infer a different grasp pose or contact region.

The retrieval_description will be converted into a text embedding and used to
retrieve surfaces with similar pad-to-material interfaces. Keep it concise and
discriminating.

Describe only properties of the material that actually touches the pads: the
substrate; any coating, label, wrapper, sleeve, or finish covering it; relevant
visible texture, porosity, or apparent compliance; and visible condition such as
clean, dry, dusty, wet, oily, worn, or unknown. If the material, coating, or
condition is ambiguous, state that uncertainty rather than inventing it.

Do not mention object identity, branding, color, size, shape, pose, grasp
orientation, curvature, contact region, local geometry, edges, openings, or overall
surface area. Do not recommend a gripper, predict force, infer a force label, or
restate measured mass, measured roughness index, or projected contact fraction.
descriptor.instruction:
Inspect the photographed pad-contact surface and return the requested structured
JSON with:
- the material actually touching the pads, distinguishing the substrate from any
  label, wrapper, coating, sleeve, finish, or exposed contents;
- the visible material and surface condition;
- whether the material properties are clearly visible;
- uncertainty limited to material, coating, finish, or condition identification;
- a single concise retrieval_description sentence containing only the most
  discriminating pad-to-material interface properties.

Use this retrieval_description format:
"[Contact material or substrate] with [coating or finish if present] and [visible
material condition or interface property]."

Good retrieval_description examples:
1. "Clean, dry glass contact surface with a smooth nonporous finish and no visible
   coating or contamination."
2. "Dry woven textile contact surface with a compliant fibrous texture and no
   visible moisture or loose debris."
3. "Clean, dry paperboard contact surface with a thin matte printed coating over a
   rigid fibrous substrate."

Do not mention the object name or type, branding, color, shape, size, curvature,
pose, grasp orientation, contact region, local geometry, edges, openings, contact
area, mass, measured roughness, or projected contact fraction. Do not choose gecko
or silicone and do not estimate force. Return only JSON matching the supplied
schema.

gecko.description: Parallel-jaw gripper with two opposing, rigid fingers. One finger is stationary, while the other translates laterally toward it to close around an object positioned between them. Each finger carries an inward-facing, mushroom-tipped gecko-inspired dry-adhesive pad of length 4.2 inches mounted on a rigid backing. The fingers and adhesive backings remain rigid during grasping and do not conform to the object. Therefore, the maximum adhesion requires the object’s opposing sidewalls to be sufficiently flat, parallel, and aligned with the pads so that broad contact can form. Generally, the greater the adhesion, the lower the grasp force required to pick up the object. Dry adhesion performs best on clean, dry, smooth, nonporous surfaces and degrades with roughness, porosity, contamination, moisture, and loose coatings. On objects that are incompatible with dry adhesion, limited frictional support still applies; thus, the gecko-adhesive-based gripper can technically still grasp the objects; however, gecko should be fully avoided for greasy, dusty, and sharp objects.

assumptions_and_uncertainty: No authoritative mass or friction coefficient was provided, introducing visual estimation uncertainty

Thus, a force of 5.5 N is estimated.
